Through theoretical analysis, the authors demonstrate that the imaginary component's sine-based characteristic curve allows it to attend more to distant positions, complementing the real component's cosine-based curve. Empirically, the paper evaluates RoPE++ on both short- and long-context benchmarks, demonstrating consistent performance improvements over standard RoPE, particularly as the context length increases. The results show that RoPE++ not only enhances long-context performance but also offers efficiency gains, especially with RoPE++<sub>EH</sub>, which reduces memory cost and speeds up decoding. The paper also provides insights into the attention patterns of real and imaginary components, showing that the imaginary component plays a dominant role in capturing long-range dependencies. The authors claim that the code and checkpoints will be released, which is crucial for reproducibility and adoption by the community.
